source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study
finding: Blinded expert reviewers rated LLM-agent research ideas as more novel than ideas written by expert humans. Feasibility was slightly lower.
numbers: 49 human writers, 79 reviewers. Novelty means: human 4.84 (n=119 reviews), AI 5.64 (n=109), AI + human rerank 5.81 (n=109). Excitement: 4.55, 5.19, 5.46. Feasibility: human 6.61, AI 6.34 (not significant).
limits: Novelty judged by experts is noisy. Only NLP prompting topics. The AI pipeline already contains generate-then-filter stages.
agent_relevance: Loose mass generation followed by a control stage works: the winning arm over-generated, deduplicated, then ranked. This matches the two-phase pattern (generate, then evaluate).

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study - diversity of generation
finding: Over-generation by an LLM saturates. Most newly generated ideas repeat earlier ones.
numbers: Out of 4000 generated seed ideas per topic only about 200 were non-duplicates (cosine similarity threshold 0.8, all-MiniLM-L6-v2), about 5%. Non-duplicate share per batch keeps falling and the cumulative count plateaus.
limits: One embedding model and one threshold. Topic-level average.
agent_relevance: The loose phase has a ceiling. More samples from one model do not give more distinct ideas. Add diversity forcing (different seeds, constraints), not just more draws. Supports G4.

source: Si, Yang, Hashimoto (2024) Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study - LLM as evaluator
finding: LLM judges are poor at ranking ideas. This is the weak spot of the control phase when the model does the controlling.
numbers: Human inter-reviewer consistency 56.1% (balanced accuracy, top and bottom 25%). Best LLM judge (Claude-3.5 pairwise ranker) 53.3%; GPT-4o direct 50.0%, pairwise 45.0%; Claude-3.5 direct 51.7%; AI-Scientist reviewer 43.3%. Claude-3.5 got 71.4% on accepted vs rejected paper pairs (GPT-4o 61.1%).
limits: Small test set. Idea ranking is hard even for humans (ICLR'24 reviewers 71.9% on their own metric).
agent_relevance: In a loose-then-control agent the inhibition/evaluation step should use code checks or external grounding, not LLM self-ranking. Supports G5.

source: Yao et al. (2023) Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
finding: A scaffold that proposes several thoughts and then has the model evaluate and prune them (generate then control) beat plain chain of thought on Game of 24. It is the closest engineering analogue of DMN generation plus ECN evaluation.
numbers: Game of 24 (GPT-4): IO 7.3%, CoT 4.0%, CoT-SC k=100 9.0%, ToT b=1 45%, ToT b=5 74%. Creative Writing coherence (GPT-4 score, 100 tasks): IO 6.19, CoT 6.93, ToT 7.56.
limits: Evaluator is the same model, so errors correlate. Math has a checkable answer; writing coherence is LLM-scored. Many more calls.
agent_relevance: Two phases with a cheap evaluator between them is a documented pattern. For our schema the evaluator should be code where possible (G5).

source: Lu et al. (2025) Benchmarking Language Model Creativity: A Case Study on Code Generation (NeoCoder, NeoGauge, Denial Prompting)
finding: Divergent and convergent creativity trade off in LLMs. Forcing new solutions by stacking constraints (Denial Prompting) lowers correctness, and GPT-4 reaches zero combined creativity at constraint level 5.
numbers: GPT-4, constraint state t=0..5: pass@1 16.1, 11.6, 7.1, 5.2, 2.3, 2.1; divergent creative 4.5, 11.9, 11.5, 12.4, 13.2, 15.3; convergent creative 16.2, 8.1, 3.6, 1.6, 0.0, 0.0; NeoGauge@5 = 0. GPT-4 most creative of 8+ models, still below humans.
limits: Code only (Codeforces). Sampling temperature 1.
agent_relevance: Generating differently and being right pull apart. A control phase that rewards only correctness kills novelty; one that rewards only novelty fails correctness. Keep both scores separate.

source: Lu et al. (2025) NeoCoder - reasoning strategies
finding: Strategies built to raise accuracy did little for creativity. Only tree search (MCTS) raised divergent output, and it did not raise the combined score.
numbers: MCTS re-evaluated on CodeGemma-7B; self-correction, planning and sampling on GPT-3.5. All but sampling raised convergent creativity; only MCTS raised divergent creativity in all 5 states; its NeoGauge gain was minimal and 0 after t=2.
limits: Small models for MCTS; GPT-3.5 for the others.
agent_relevance: Single-path refinement (self-correction) does not widen search. Breadth must come from the generation phase.

source: Lu et al. (2024) LLM Discussion: Enhancing the Creativity of LLMs via Discussion Framework and Role-Play
finding: A three-phase multi-agent framework (diverge, discuss, converge) with assigned roles raised originality and elaboration over single agent, LLM Debate and brainstorm-then-select on four creativity tests.
numbers: Benchmarks: Alternative Uses, Instances, Similarities, Scientific Creativity. Human evaluation 1,406 ratings; LLM Discussion won Originality and Elaboration on 3 of 4 benchmarks (table text garbled in PDF extraction, per-cell means not recorded).
limits: Role-play personas: our G4 says persona voters share one model's blind spots. LLM judges used; agreement with humans reported as Kendall tau.
agent_relevance: Explicit diverge-then-converge phases help on creativity tests, but part of the gain comes from roles. Treat as [S].

source: Meincke, Mollick, Terwiesch (2024) Prompting Diverse Ideas: Increasing AI Idea Variance
finding: Plain GPT-4 brainstorming pools are less diverse than human groups. Prompt structure raises diversity; chain-of-thought (break the task into steps) was among the best.
numbers: Mean pairwise cosine similarity: human groups 0.243; GPT-4 pools 0.255 to 0.432; baseline 0.377; Steve-Jobs persona 0.368; HBR creativity tools 0.387. Unique ideas in domain: about 3700 (base) vs 4700 (CoT). 35 prompts compared.
limits: Single product-idea domain; GPT-4 only; unique-idea count depends on a dedup rule.
agent_relevance: Staged generation (several micro-steps) widens the loose phase better than personas. Persona gains were tiny here, consistent with G4.

source: Doshi and Hauser (2024) Generative AI enhances individual creativity but reduces collective diversity
finding: Humans given LLM story ideas wrote more novel, more useful stories, but the stories became more alike. Anchoring on the AI idea is the mechanism.
numbers: N=293 writers, 600 evaluators. Novelty +6.7% (b=0.259, p=0.001, human-only mean 3.85); usefulness +6.4% (b=0.319, p<0.001). With 5 ideas: novelty +8.1%, usefulness +9.0%. Story similarity to the AI idea +5.2% (human-only mean 82.85). Similarity to the group mean rose (b=0.871, p<0.001).
limits: Short 8-sentence stories; one platform; human subjects, not agents.
agent_relevance: An agent that anchors on its first generated candidate cuts the variance of its own search. Seed the loose phase with independent draws, not a shared starter.

source: Padmakumar and He (2024) Does Writing with Language Models Reduce Content Diversity?
finding: Co-writing with a feedback-tuned model (InstructGPT) homogenised essays; co-writing with base GPT-3 did not. The loss came from the model's contributions, not the users'.
numbers: 38 Upwork writers, three groups (solo, GPT-3, InstructGPT). InstructGPT essays were most similar to each other and lowest in lexical and content diversity; GPT-3 group not significantly different from solo.
limits: Small N; argumentative essays; one 2022 model pair.
agent_relevance: Alignment tuning narrows the loose phase. Prefer base-like sampling for generation and apply control later.

source: Mohammadi (2024) Creativity Has Left the Chat: The Price of Debiasing Language Models
finding: RLHF-aligned Llama-2 models show lower token entropy, tight clusters in embedding space, and return to 'attractor states' after perturbation, compared with base models.
numbers: Three experiments, Llama-2 base vs aligned chat; aligned model favoured a few names ('Emily', 'Samantha'); base model had significantly higher average token entropy.
limits: One model family; marketing tasks; effect sizes not extracted from the PDF.
agent_relevance: Alignment weakens the DMN-like loose generator. If the agent needs variety, sample from higher-entropy settings or a less aligned drafting pass.

source: Peeperkorn et al. (2024) Is Temperature the Creativity Parameter of LLMs?
finding: Temperature is a weak lever for creativity. It correlates weakly with novelty, moderately with incoherence, and not with typicality or cohesion.
numbers: Narrative generation with fixed model, context and prompt; four conditions: novelty, typicality, cohesion, coherence. Exact correlation values not extracted (table not parsed).
limits: One model, one narrative task.
agent_relevance: Random noise is not DMN-style associative retrieval. Raising temperature alone buys little; structured variation (constraints, reframing) is needed.

source: Jiang et al. (2025/2026) Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models
finding: Across 70+ models, answers to open-ended questions are similar within one model and across models. Models, reward models and LLM judges are poorly calibrated to human ratings on responses that split human opinion.
numbers: INFINITY-CHAT with 26K real prompts; 31,250 human annotations. For 100 queries x 50 responses at top-p 0.9, temperature 1.0, mean within-prompt pairwise similarity typically above 0.8; still above 0.8 at min-p 0.1, temperature 2.0. DeepSeek-V3 vs qwen-max similarity 0.82; vs gpt-4o 0.81. Random pairs 0.1 to 0.2.
limits: Embedding similarity is a proxy. The 26K figure is from the paper's abstract/intro as I read it; confirm before quoting.
agent_relevance: The loose phase of one model is narrow, and a different model gives the same answers (G4). Real variety needs external input or structural constraint.

source: Chakrabarty et al. (2024) Art or Artifice? LLMs and the False Promise of Creativity (TTCW)
finding: Expert writers using 14 binary Torrance-style tests found LLM stories pass 3 to 10 times fewer tests than professional stories. LLM judges did not correlate positively with experts.
numbers: 10 creative writers, 48 stories (professional vs LLM); LLM assessors showed no positive correlation with expert assessment.
limits: Abstract and intro read; tables not extracted. Models are 2023 vintage.
agent_relevance: Reinforces that LLM-as-evaluator of creative quality is unreliable. Use external or code-based checks.

source: Mischler et al. (2024) Contextual Feature Extraction Hierarchies Converge in LLMs and the Brain
finding: Better LLMs map more closely onto the brain's hierarchical language pathway using fewer layers. This is about speech and language areas (neurosurgical recordings), not the DMN/ECN creativity network.
numbers: Intracranial recordings from patients listening to speech; higher benchmark performance gave higher brain similarity.
limits: Language cortex only. No creativity or network-level test. No study I could open maps the creativity network model onto transformer layers.
agent_relevance: Do not borrow a DMN-to-attention-head mapping. Brain alignment evidence covers language processing, not the generate/control loop.

source: Huang, Liu, Yang (2026) Evaluation of LLMs as Tools, Models, and Partners in Creative Thinking Research (GCA framework review)
finding: Review of Jan 2018 to Jun 2026: LLMs exceed average human performance on divergent thinking in most independent comparisons, with a fluency dependency, a human advantage at the top end, and a novelty-typicality trade-off. No evidence that LLMs instantiate human-like creative mechanisms.
numbers: Hedges g 0.5 to 2.6. Table 2: Hubert 2024 AUT originality g=2.61 [2.30,2.91] (post hoc fluency match), elaboration 4.07; Koivisto and Grassini 2023 AUT originality 0.70 [0.33,1.06] (prospective fluency match); Bellemare-Pepin 2026 DAT vs population 0.52 [0.39,0.64], vs top 50% of humans -0.88 (human advantage). Automated scoring ICC>=0.80, r>=0.70 in selected studies.
limits: Narrative review, not pre-registered; effect sizes recomputed by the authors; training-data contamination possible, so upper bounds.
agent_relevance: Average-level LLM originality is not the target; the agent's weakness is peak and diversity. Report fluency-matched numbers.

source: Huang et al. (2026) GCA review - network frame for LLMs
finding: The review uses the DMN/ECN/salience account as a heuristic frame for LLMs: self-attention and decoding are likened to spreading activation and to executive modulation of default output. It also lists limits: LLMs lack insight, incubation and conscious evaluation.
numbers: Mapping given as analogy only; cites Beaty 2018, Benedek and Fink 2019, Lloyd-Cox 2022. Notes transformer attention is deterministic over a fixed window, human activation is recurrent and stochastic.
limits: Analogy, no measured test of the mapping.
agent_relevance: Our two-phase scaffold borrows the idea, not any brain evidence about LLMs. Label it [D] design choice.

source: Hubert et al. (2024) Current state of AI generative language models is more creative than humans on divergent thinking tasks (as summarised in Huang 2026)
finding: GPT-4 beat 151 humans on AUT, Consequences and DAT. Known here only through the 2026 review; the original paper was not opened.
numbers: 151 humans; AUT originality g=2.61 and elaboration g=4.07 per review recalculation, post hoc fluency matching.
limits: Original blocked (Nature redirect). Post hoc matching inflates the gap versus prospective matching.
agent_relevance: Treat the size as an upper bound.

source: Koivisto and Grassini (2023) Best humans still outperform AI in a creative divergent thinking task (as summarised in Huang 2026)
finding: Average LLM originality beats average human, but the top humans still exceed the best LLM outputs. Seen only via the review.
numbers: AUT originality g=0.70 [0.33,1.06] under prospective fluency matching.
limits: Original not opened.
agent_relevance: A peak-creativity gap supports keeping external search or humans in the loop for rare ideas.

source: Organisciak et al. (2023) Beyond semantic distance: automated scoring of divergent thinking improves with LLMs (as summarised in Huang 2026)
finding: Fine-tuned LLM scoring of originality beat older semantic-distance scoring and agreed with expert raters. Seen only via the review.
numbers: Review reports ICC above 0.80 against expert ratings.
limits: Original not opened. Task-specific; generalisation across languages untested.
agent_relevance: A trained scorer can serve as the evaluator, but test it on our domain first (G3).

source: Kenett, Yoed et al. (2025) Dynamic switching between brain networks predicts creative ability
finding: Largest creativity-network study: the count of DMN-ECN switches in resting-state fMRI predicts divergent thinking but not general intelligence. The relation is an inverted U with balance of switching.
numbers: 10 independent samples (Austria, Canada, China, Japan, US), N=2433; independent task-fMRI validation N=31 showed higher DMN-ECN switching during idea generation than control and replicated the inverted U.
limits: Resting-state predictor; correlational. Abstract and introduction read; effect sizes not extracted.
agent_relevance: Supports alternation between loose and control phases, with an optimal middle: neither all-loose nor all-control. Switch count and balance are testable design variables.

source: Neural dynamics during the generation and evaluation of creative and non-creative ideas (2025)
finding: Generation and evaluation of ideas recruit different dynamic patterns across executive, default and salience networks. Dynamic network measures differed from task-free rest.
numbers: Two fMRI sessions a week apart: generate creative or non-creative uses (session 1), evaluate own responses (session 2). Rest whole-brain reconfiguration mean 0.543 (SD 0.085), lower than all four task conditions.
limits: Only the abstract and one results passage read; N not extracted.
agent_relevance: Evidence that generate and evaluate are separable stages in humans, backing our two-state split.

source: Horowitz-Kraus et al. (2026) Lower engagement of cognitive control in children on ChatGPT
finding: fMRI during a 5-minute co-creative dialog with ChatGPT: adults show stronger within-network frontoparietal, salience and dorsal attention connectivity and more cross-network coupling than children. Creativity scores did not differ.
numbers: 15 first graders (mean age 6.44) and 16 adults (mean 38.12); seven networks including default, salience, frontoparietal; adult-greater FP-salience and FP-DAN coupling.
limits: Tiny samples; naturalistic, uncontrolled dialogue. The only study found that scans humans using an LLM and reports network results.
agent_relevance: Control networks matter in using an LLM well; a scaffold that supplies control may help weak controllers. Similar scores with different neural profiles.

source: Flow-state review (2025): enhanced DMN-ECN connectivity during flow, creativity and emotional regulation
finding: Across nine studies, flow shows reduced core DMN activity, more lateral prefrontal and parietal activity, and coupling between networks that normally anticorrelate.
numbers: PRISMA review, 9 studies (video games to jazz improvisation).
limits: Small, heterogeneous set; abstract read only.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: some creative states have loose and control networks active together, not in sequence. Our two-phase split may be a simplification.

source: Beaty, Seli, Schacter (2019) Network neuroscience of creative cognition (Curr Opin Behav Sci)
finding: Review in the key-work slot. Not opened this session. Its claim, as used by the 2026 review, is that DMN, executive control and salience networks cooperate during creative thought.
numbers: No numbers recorded (not opened).
limits: Not opened this session.
agent_relevance: Placeholder only; use the human-side evidence files for the data.

source: Beaty et al. (2018) Robust prediction of individual creative ability from brain functional connectivity (PNAS)
finding: Connectome-based prediction of divergent-thinking ability from connectivity among DMN, ECN and salience regions. The PNAS page returned HTTP 403, so details are unverified.
numbers: Not recorded (page not opened).
limits: Not opened; do not quote numbers from memory.
agent_relevance: Cited by the 2026 review as the main basis for the DMN/ECN/salience heuristic.

source: Gap statement: no study found that scans LLM internals or tests a DMN/ECN analogue in an LLM agent loop
url: Semantic Scholar, arXiv API and OpenAlex were rate-limited; WebSearch budget exhausted
finding: Within what I could reach, no paper directly tests a DMN/ECN-style two-network architecture inside an LLM. Closest are generate/evaluate scaffolds (ToT), diverge/converge pipelines (LLM Discussion, Si et al.), and brain-alignment studies of language cortex only.
numbers: Zero direct hits; coverage limited by tool failures, so absence is weak evidence.
limits: Search was incomplete.
agent_relevance: Do not claim neuroscience backing for the scaffold's two phases beyond analogy.
